question.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1}$ and ${X}_{2}$ are independent random variables, where ${X}_{1}∼N({\mu }_{1},{\sigma }_{1}^{2})$ and ${X}_{2}∼N({\mu }_{2},{\sigma }_{2}^{2}),$ and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then 

$$
a{X}_{1}+b{X}_{2}∼N(a{\mu }_{1}+b{\mu }_{2},{a}^{2}{\sigma }_{1}^{2}+{b}^{2}{\sigma }_{2}^{2}).
$$

Since ${X}_{1}$ and ${X}_{2}$ are independent, the distribution of $Y$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Y={X}_{1}+{X}_{2} & ∼N({\mu }_{1}+{\mu }_{2},{\sigma }_{1}^{2}+{\sigma }_{2}^{2}) \\  & ∼N(-14-6,400+225) \\  & ∼N(-20,625).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $Y$ is normally distributed with mean $\mu =-20$ and standard deviation $\sigma =\sqrt{625}=25.$ 

We want to find $P(-28<Y\le 12).$ Thus, we convert $Y$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-28<Y\le 12) & =P(\frac{-28+20}{25}<Z\le \frac{12+20}{25}) \\  & =P(-0.32\le Z\le 1.28) \\  & =P(Z<1.28)-P(Z<-0.32) \\  & =Φ(1.28)-Φ(-0.32)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-0.32) & ≈0.3745 \\ Φ(1.28) & ≈0.8997.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-28<Y\le 12) & =Φ(1.28)-Φ(-0.32) \\  & ≈0.8997-0.3745 \\  & ≈0.53.\end{aligned}
$$
